subject: Repost: Necromancer is a kind of warlock...
content_md:
Blizzard's original warlock specs are more inclined to three different styles of the class as a demon summoner, which in fact is a system varying only on the extent of demon's participation in combat. In other words, the affliction warlock is merely a lesser demon summoner than demonological warlocks. In my opinion, that sounds like a controvercial identity of affliction warlocks regarding whether they are dark spell casters who can also summon demons or demon summoners who use weak demons (or a shadow priest who uses demons).

My suggestion is transmogging affliction to necromance by replacing demon minions with undead creatures. It doesn't feel odd that a warlock (dark caster) can control skeletons or ghouls. They can only operate in shadow, away from the public, and necromance has been extant in Warcraft prior to the founding of the Cult of the Damned, so the change would cause no contradiction to the basic plot.

Destrucion spec, just like Affliction, could be revamped. Into a Old God-affiliated summoner maybe.

Overall, I suggest that warlocks exist in game as a light armored summoner of diversified evils.

subject: Warlock talent and spell reworks wishlist
content_md:
Hello folks!

So i've been trying to compile some sort of wish list for some changes for warlocks with a few other very active warlocks in the community. The point of this list is to express some opinions of the warlock community in regards to its state, and offer some suggestions in order to try to push the class towards a better spot in the game overall, because, as we probably know, currently, warlocks are struggling in raiding environments overall compared to other pure damage classes that tend to get a much better deal out of an easier gameplay loop on top of it.

Moreover, i know not everyone would always agree with every suggested change, and i myself in no way am trying to pretend to be the ultimate expert at the class, i certainly have a lots of things to learn from much better players than me. All that to say, feel free to disagree (respectfully!) with anything in this list.

So, here are the suggestions we came up with:

 1. Sinister Pursuit: removed. Comment: there are enough filler talents in the affliction tree as is, this talent has no practical purpose at all in any area of the game. Edit after comments: instead of this talent, make it a Grimoire to be bought from the demon trainers that permanently increases the demons' movement speed by 10 or 15%.

 2. New talent (Destruction tree, row 1): a 3 point talent that reduces the warlock's (and the demon's) generated threat by 10% per point. Comment: most of caster classes / specs have threat reduction talents (except elemental shamans and moonkins, and that fact is also sometimes an issue for them), while warlocks have only some small threat reduction effects scattered between Voidstone's 10% reduction, and sacrificed succubus' 10% reduction, both of which options reduce the build diversity quite a lot if they get mandatory to have.

 3. As a followup to #2, rework Create Voidstone to now grant 2% cast speed.

 4. As a followup to #2, rework the Demonic Sacrifice's talent's bonuses. Suggestions: Imp: Increases the casting speed by 4%. Succubus: Increases spell critical strike chance by 4%.

 5. Aftermath: removed. Replaced by: 3 point talent, grants 2% spell hit per point for destruction spells. Comment: Aftermath is a very poor talent that offers very little to Immolate's damage over time only, and very inconsistent CC, so both of these effects can be moved elsewhere; destruction warlocks have a harder time than affliction gearing up in earlier raids with no spell hit talent support, this would help them in that regard. Rebalance a few T3.5 destruction gear pieces by removing some spell hit and incrasing spell damage or adding spell crit instead.

 6. Resilient Shadows: buff it from 5% chance for affliction spells to not be dispelled per point to a much higher value, like 20% or 25% per point. Comment: affliction warlocks' damage is based on damage over time effects and they tend to get totally shut down when facing a dispell class. If necessary, move this talent in a deeper row in the Affliction tree, for example instead of Grim Reach or Soul Siphon.

 7. Shadow Mastery: reworked. Now instead of increasing the damage dealt or life drained by shadow spells by 10%, increases the damage over time of Affliction spells by 25% (5% per point). Comment: Affliction's damage over time effects should deal noticeably more damage than non affliction trees, which historically has not really been the case.

 8. Curse of Agony: now deals constant damage over time on every tick, instead of ramping its damage per tick. The total damage dealt by the curse remains the same. Comment: see the suggested Dark Harvest's rework, right below.

 9. Dark Harvest: reworked. Now, haste increases the cooldown recovery of this spell. Moreover, instead of accelerating all damage over time effects by 30% during its channeling, this spell instead refreshes all damage over time durations of Affliction damage over time spells on its last tick. Comment: this spell in its current implementation has received too much of a mixed reception in regards to its power, with the overwhelming opinion of it needing to be a better capstone spell for Affliction.

 10. Health Funnel and Mana Funnel start their first tick instantly. Comment: the first tick should happen instantly instead of after 1s as it is currently, we already have 1.5s GCD that limits the spammability of these spells, as well as health and mana initial upfront costs.

 11. Rain of Fire: increase the spell damage scaling.

 12. Hellfire: increase the spell damage scaling, each tick of this spell can now be a critical hit, similar to how Arcane Missiles' channels work for mages. Comment: the steep mana cost, the damage taken, the fact the caster has to stay immobile and the fact the caster has to stay in melee range of the enemies to affect them with this spell is enough reasons to make this spell deal significantly more damage.

 13. Improved Soul Fire: instead of increasing your fire damage by 10% for 30s, now increase the damage of all destruction spells by 10% for 30s. Comment: the destruction tree focuses too much on fire damage, while Shadow Bolt is part of the Destruction spell school and hence, should also count for this talent.

 14. Emberstorm: instead of increasing the damage of fire spells by 10% for 5 points, instead, increase the damage of all destruction spells by 10% for 5 points. Comment: see comment on #13.

 15. Searing Pain: increase its spell damage scaling coefficient in order to make this a better filler option. If necessary, increase its cast time by 0.5s.

 16. Intensity: instead of giving Fire spells only a chance to not lose casting time when taking damage, make it apply to all Destruction spells. Comment: see comment #13.

 17. Master Demonologist: Greater Demons: reduce the healing received by 40% for 5 points except from the Warlock's healing effects. Comment: Felstone and vampirism effects should be a good option to heal greater demons, and not also get nerfed by 40%.

 18. Ritual of Doom: reworked to now not need additional summoners anymore.

 19. Master Summoner: now also reduces the cooldown of Ritual of Doom by 50% when 2 points allocated in the talent.

 20. Curse of Doom: reworked to explode after 15s instead of after 1 min, remove its cooldown. Scale down its damage accordingly.

 21. Fel Stamina is now a 3 point talent, rather than a 5 point talent.

 22. Demonic Aegis: removed. Demon Armor's baseline bonuses are buffed. Instead, Demonic Swiftness (from destruction tree) takes its place.

 23. New talent in demonology tree, 5th row: Your Curse of Doom can be used alongside other curses. Applying Curse of Recklessness, Curse of Shadow or Curse of Elements also afflicts the target with your highest rank of Curse of Doom.

 24. Nightfall: also reduces the mana cost of Shadow Bolts from this effect by 50%.

 25. Create Firestone: instead of granting 2% critical chance to your Fire spells, grant that to all Destruction spells. Comment: see comment #13.

 26. Unleashed Potential: also grants the warlock a debuff that does nothing but that lasts for the same duration as the Unleashed Potential's buff duration on the current demon. Comment: demonology warlock is notorious for its lack of quality of life when it comes to managing the pets, and the tracking of the Unleashed Potential stacks's duration is part of the problem. Moreover, i know not everyone would always agree with every suggested change, and i myself in no way am trying to pretend to be the ultimate expert at the class, i certainly have a lots of things to learn from much better players than me. 1. Sinister Pursuit: removed. Comment: there are enough filler talents in the affliction tree as is, this talent has no practical purpose at all in any area of the game. 3. As a followup to #2, rework Create Voidstone to now grant 2% cast speed.

4. As a followup to #2, rework the Demonic Sacrifice's talent's bonuses. Suggestions: Imp: Increases the casting speed by 4%. Succubus: Increases spell critical strike chance by 4%.

5. Aftermath: removed. Replaced by: 3 point talent, grants 2% spell hit per point for destruction spells. Comment: affliction warlocks' damage is based on damage over time effects and they tend to get totally shut down when facing a dispell class. 7. Shadow Mastery: reworked. Now instead of increasing the damage dealt or life drained by shadow spells by 10%, increases the damage over time of Affliction spells by 25% (5% per point). I was having a conversation about Warlock tweaks that would be nice and decided to chime in on this topic rather than make my own.

 - I agree with ideas regarding the use of Stones needing to be instant cast.  Keep the creation of them the same, but being able to swap between Stones should be something situationally rewarding to Warlocks.

As for the specific suggestions I have:

 1. Firestone giving essentially a Fiery Weapon enchant to melee attacks is weird.  There is something there, but you need a rework of Firestone.  Keep the +Crit to Fire Spells, but perhaps give Melee Crits a chance to make Searing Pain Instant Cast - but to make that possible you would also need to have Firestone give Warlocks Melee Hit equal to their Spell Hit.

 2. Spellstone.  Spellstones share a CD with Healthstones.  Spellstones absorb incoming Magic Damage, but the damage they absorb is less than the health that a Healthstone heals.  So being a better player and anticipating incoming damage is not rewarded as much as being braindead and healing after taking damage.
 - Spellstone suggestion 1 - Spellstones restore mana equal to 50% of spell damage absorbed.
 - Spellstone suggestion 2 - Spellstones give a 30 second buff of 30 to magic resistance of the type of magic damage absorbed (absorb fire damage, gain fire resistance) - might be harder to code this one though.

 3. I like Szalord's idea about Voidstones giving a 2% bonus to casting speed.
 - A second suggestion I might have would be that while using Voidstones Warlocks are immune to magic reflect causing their spells to come back at them.

 4. Wrathstone - I kind of like the double-edged sword of Wrathstone.  It's great to be able to deal more threat, and it's also great to take less damage from hellfire - but Hellfire threat is dangerous enough without Wrathstone - with Wrathstone it's downright deadly.
 - Maybe Wrathstones should synergize with the idea of Fire and Threat and have their own version of Malediction, where casting Immolate on a target also applies Curse of Weakness.

 5. Felstone - I think there is room for more Demon Synergy here.  Because Felstone heals the Warlock and their Pet for damage done by the Warlock - but perhaps that buff should apply to the Demon as well.

As much as I would love to see a Demon Within build added to Demonology, I know that's kind of unrealistic - but the function of Warlock Stones really needs some work if we want them to be more than just "situationally useful".

About two weeks ago there was a change in enslaved demon behavior, including greater demon pets (infernal, felguard, doomguard).

content_md:
Saw this reddit post and i think its well made and should be shared here on the forum.

That's how I plan to level, maybe it'll help someone. This is strictly PvE, I'll add some remarks here and there about PvP but I'm a noob in that space so keep that in mind.

How rotation looks like/the playstyle of affliction leveling:

Corruption -> curse of agony -> drain soul/drain life/dark harvest (on tougher mobs) -> shadow bolt whenever you get a nightfall proc. Warlocks can relatively easily "juggle" 2-3 mobs at a time; applying DoTs on all mobs, fearing one mob, tanking the second, pet handling the third. Keep in mind that with the changes to fel concentration, AoE fearing with howl of terror would be much easier.

 **The leveling build:** [https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... BFAB-AoD-F](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c/1.18.0/warlock?points=EoASCASDJBFAB-AoD-F)

 10-14: improved corruption 5/5

 15-17: suppression 3/5

 18-19: improved life tap 2/2 *I prefer the hit chance first but you can easily do lifetap before suppression, or, 2 points suppression -> 2 points life tap -> 1 point suppression.

 20-21: fel concentration 2/2

 22-23: improved drains 2/2

 24: suppression 4/5 OR improved curse of agony 1/3 BUT if you plan to PvP I would definitely take curse of exhaustion 1/1.

 25: nightfall 1/2

 26-28: soul siphon 3/3

 29: nightfall 2/2

 30: malediction 1/1 *if you plan to PvP, I would take improved curse of exhaustion around these levels.

 31: siphon life 1/1 *these last two picks are interchangeable, I prefer the QoL of malediction first, also, from previous leveling I found siphon life to be overkill for most mobs (corruption + agony + drains is more than enough to kill a mob and putting siphon life on top of all these usually ends up being mana wasteful. YMMV.)

 32: rapid deterioration 1/2

 33-34: grim reach 2/2

 35-39: shadow mastery 5/5

 40: dark harvest 1/1

 41-45: shadow vulnerability (destruction tree)

 46-50: demonic embrace 5/5 (demonology tree)

 51-53: demonic aegis (demonology tree)

The last 7 points are up to you, some good options are: master conjurer, improved curse of agony, finishing suppression, curse of exhaustion & improved curse of exhaustion, finishing rapid deterioration, shadowburn for even more damage, fel domination and fel stamina.

Pets:

For solo leveling I'd suggest either a succubus or a voidwalker. Try them both out and see which one fits your playstyle better. Succubus is more damage, voidwalker is more tankiness. Keep in mind that the voidwalker threat ability upgrades every ten levels (10, 20, etc) so it might be decent at holding threat when it gets a new rank and terrible at levels 17-19, 27-29, etc when you continuously keep gaining power but it still uses the same threat rank power for almost ten levels (similar to hunter pets growl).

For dungeons and group play I'd use imp since it gives a stamina buff to the entire party. If you see the tank is struggling to hold aggro on several target pulls, you could offer them to off-tank a target with your voidwalker. If there's more than one warlock in the party one should use imp and the other(s) a succubus for more damage.

The beauty of warlock pets is that they are your minions that you can summon and dispose of as you please and as the situation calls.

author: Sleeplust
subject: Demonic Sacrifice should be displaced or redesigned
content_md:
This talent, Demonic Sacrifice, has a long history. Initially, or in early game, it is a relatively deeper talent that exists as the prerequisite passer-by investment for the more significant Soul Link. There have been a number of strategies or popular talent builds involving the effect of demonic sacrifice since 2004. And now in early 2026, TWoW has moved this talent to a shallower deck, with a deck 1 talent as its prerequisite. These two talents stack as a 10% increase to all warlock spells' damage when the imp is sacrificed.

The first problem is still about its strategic inclination - discarding a demon and fighting alone, which is contradictive to the minion-based style of Demonology spec. I think its initial form in vanilla is a better design as a minor option that can be adopted when in need.

The second problem is that this talent is actually too essential with an effect similar to some much deeper ones like Shadow Mastery and Ember Storm, which also requires at least 5 talent points for 10% of a specific spell damage (shadow or fire). As a DPS in a Naxx raid, a Affliction or Destruction warlock typically needs this talent to maximise the damage. Ironically, a demonology warlock doesn't. In other words, if you want to benefit the raid with a blood pact from your imp, you need to reduce your max damage by nearly 10%. If you want to tank Vek'lor, you can take the imp for higher HP, but your threat will be reduced.

The possible redesign: make this talent split into corresponding demons' skill lists, such as binding it to the voidwalker's damage absorbing shield and making it an burst damaging skill and you would never need the effect of this talent all the time.

author: Spritzbube
subject: Re: Warlocks Affliction Build is OP
content_md:
The problem isn’t that Affliction is too strong — the real issue is that the other builds (SM/Ruin and Fire) are simply too weak.

Fire has some potential, but Searing Pain is just a bad filler spell, and the threat generation is way too high. Some fire warlocks are even casting Shadow Bolts in a fire spec, which is honestly ridiculous. On top of that, getting hit-capped without any talent support is extremely difficult unless you already have specific items from  MC/BWL/AQ40/Naxx (and yes you need to farm all this raids for specific items). That makes Fire mostly a PvP or very late-game option.

SM/Ruin, on the other hand, is just in a terrible spot right now. It doesn’t perform at all and feels completely underwhelming.

Affliction is harder to execute properly, but gearing for it is much easier thanks to the 10% hit from talents. All you need is 5-6% hit and as much haste as you can get and it performs really well. That said, I think Dark Harvest should simply function as a stronger version of Drain Soul. Managing a proper rotation with Dark Harvest alongside all the DoTs is already extremely demanding, and compared to other classes, Affliction is more than challenging enough to play effectively.

In my opinion, Fire should get a hit talent and a buff to Searing Pain. For example, swapping the Searing Pain crit talent to a hit talent and increasing its spell power scaling (as they’re apparently planning in the new patch) would already make a big difference. But without a threat reduction talent I feel, it would still perform worse than affliction.
